newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CROESUS TO RAISE BINDULI GOLD OUTPUT.
newsitem.headline: CROESUS TO RAISE BINDULI GOLD OUTPUT.

text.p: Croesus Mining NL said on Wednesday it will spend A$4.1 million to expand gold production at its Binduli mine in Western Australia by upgrading its Hannan South gold treatment plant.
The upgrade is part of a strategy to lift the mine's gold yield and reduce operating costs, the company said.
The upgrade will enable the plant, which is currently treating oxide ore, to process 500,000 tonnes of primary ore a year at an average operating cost of A$13.50 a tonne, Croesus said.

The decision to upgrade the plant was based on test drilling results that doubled the size of the high-grade eastern contact mineralisation zone in the eastern portion of the mine's Centurion pit, the company said.
The zone has registered 119,000 tonnes of ore grading 12.3 grammes of gold per tonne, or 47,000 ounces of gold, Croesus said.
The zone is the high-grade component of the the primary Centurion resource, which currently totals 146,000 ounces, the company said.
The first phase of the Centurion pit is scheduled to produce 58,000 ounces off gold at a cash operating cost of between A$320 and A$360 an ounce, Croesus said.
Production is slated to start in December and should yield about 40,000 ounces in the 1997/98 (July/June) financial year, the company said.
Croesus also said a strong gold hedging portfolio and cash and bullion reserves of A$16 million was enabling it to look at additional expansion opportunities.
It said its current forward gold sales position amounted to 92,000 ounces at an average selling price of A$611 an ounce.
This compares with a current gold price of around A$440 an ounce.
